chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sadan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Hisham ibn Salim al-Jawaliqi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Do we marry the woman for a temporary marriage that is vague/ambiguous? He said: That is more difficult for you; you inherit her and she inherits you, and it is not permissible for you to divorce her except in a state of purity with two witnesses.

I said: May God make you perfect, so how do we marry her? He said: For a specified number of days, for a specified amount, equal to what you have agreed upon. When her days are completed, her divorce is by virtue of the condition itself, and there is no maintenance (nafaqah) and no waiting period ('iddah) for her upon you.

I said: What should I say to her? He said: Say to her: I marry you upon the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Prophet, and God is my guardian and your guardian. For such and such a month, for such and such a dirham, on the condition that God guarantees for me that you will fulfill it for me, and I will not divide you (into two parts, i.e., keep one half free to marry another), nor will I claim your offspring, and there is no waiting period for you upon me. When your term expires, do not marry until forty-five nights have passed for you, and if childbirth occurs to you, inform me.

And whenever the term expires, if the man wishes to add to the term, he adds with a new contract and a new dowry, and this is not permissible for anyone else until she has completed the waiting period.

key_terms.طُهْرٍ: Purity (state of being free from menstruation/post-partum bleeding)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific legal conditions and differences between temporary marriage (mut'ah) and permanent marriage according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the mechanics of *Mut'ah* (temporary marriage) by contrasting it with permanent marriage, specifically highlighting that inheritance rights apply but formal divorce (*talaq*) is unnecessary as the contract expires automatically. It provides the precise verbal formula for the contract, noting the absence of maintenance (*nafaqah*) and the specific waiting period (*iddah*) of forty-five nights, while allowing for extension through a new contract and dowry. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in accommodating temporary unions with clear, self-executing legal boundaries.
